title: Aperture: Latency Surface & Token Flow Tiles for Per-Route Dashboards
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and prototype a compact 'Aperture' surface for per-route dashboards that surfaces multi-dimensional latency and token-flow signals in a glanceable tile grid. The surface combines a heatmap-style latency surface to compare p50/p95 across time and sequence-length buckets; token-flow micro-sparklines showing input vs output token ratios and rate; and a mini cost-lens with cost-per-1k tokens and last 24h spend trends. Intended for route owners and SREs to prioritize tuning (batching, quant profiles, routing) without digging into full trace views.
acceptance_criteria: Tile grid fits a 3-column compact dashboard row at desktop and collapses to 1 column on mobile
Latency surface shows p50 and p95 overlays and highlights anomalous cells (>2x baseline) with a side color legend
Token-flow micro-sparklines show input/output token ratio and rolling tokens/sec with hover tooltip for exact values
Mini cost-lens exposes cost-per-1k tokens and 'top contributing model' badge with link to rollout settings
Prototype includes keyboard and screen-reader accessible labels for core metrics
Design handoff includes chart spec (data schema + aggregation windows) and adaptive spacing tokens for engineering implementation
chart_spec_summary: Latency surface: 2D grid (time buckets x sequence-length buckets); cells show p50/p95 combined color and intensity; overlay marker for anomalies. Aggregation window: 1m, 5m, 1h selectable. Token-flow sparklines: dual-line (input, output) plus bar background for tokens/sec; window: 1h rolling at 10s resolution. Throughput histogram: continuous kernel density with percentile ticks. Cost-lens: numeric plus mini-trend sparkline with avg cost-per-1k computed over 24h and 7d.
engineering_notes: Expect backend time-bucketed aggregates from metric pipeline (ENG-20455)
Surface should support rapid toggles between quantized model variants (ENG-20988)
Suggestion: implement as SVG canvas with per-cell virtualization to handle long time-range queries
decisions: Chose combined p50/p95 overlay instead of side-by-side charts to save vertical space
Use sequence-length bucketing with dynamic boundaries (16,64,256,1024) rather than fixed logits to align with runtime kernel selection
Expose anomaly thresholds as dashboard-level setting (not per-tile)
tradeoffs: Overlay reduces immediate clarity for some users; we mitigate with on-hover breakdown and legends
Compact tile sacrifices full trace depth; link to microtrace explorer instead of embedding full trace
review_feedback: PM (Marco Ruiz): Add a quick action to open a canary rollout from the 'top contributing model' badge
Eng (Liang Chen): Prefer p95 focus by default for SLO-driven teams; add toggle to switch percentile baseline
Accessibility (Rita Gomez): Ensure color palette passes 4.5:1 contrast; include pattern fill fallback for printed exports
